# kfilter default policy: strict, relaxed one fatal block at a time
#
# 2026-10-31. Nothing the client does is allowed unless a rule below allows it:
# default-deny is on, there are no standing allow rules, and default-deny also
# turns off every built-in allowance (child processes from the client folder)
# and filters outside processes opening the client (csrss, the launcher, the
# elevation broker, the anti-cheat service...), which keep no access right a
# handle rule does not grant. Everything is logged: every allow (with the rule
# that allowed it) and every deny.
#
# Relaxations are counted rules, added one per run for the block that stopped
# the client, each for one exact object and exact rights:
#
#   allow|<target>|<exact path>|rights=...|uses=N[|phase=P][|opens]
#
#   uses=N   the rule allows N requests per Play, in any order; the count is
#            restored when the launch pass is armed (kfilterctl allow-launch).
#            A request that repeats is measured once (an audit rule allows and
#            records it), then tried at N-1 (must fail) and N (must pass).
#   phase=P  the rule works only once phase P is open (phase 1 is open at the
#            start); a rule marked `opens` opens the next phase on its first
#            use. Used where a run shows a reliable order.
#
# A denial of a request that a counted rule matched, after its uses were spent
# or before its phase opened, carries the EXHAUSTED flag and that rule's ID.
#
# Not covered by kfilter (outside its reach, by design of Windows): DLLs mapped
# from \KnownDlls and ntdll (no file open by the client), work other processes
# do on their own (csrss reading manifests, services the client calls over
# ALPC/RPC), and the kernel. Network: the client's own connections, listens
# and accepts are filtered (with loopback); DNS lookups are made by the DNS
# service on its behalf and are not.

mode audit

# The application the policy applies to: every Nexon program (the launcher under
# C:\Program Files (x86)\Nexon\Nexon Launcher, its Electron UI, agent and runtime; NGService
# from C:\ProgramData\Nexon\NGS and the game's grap folder; the game and its parts). Names are
# matched against the tail of the image path, case-insensitively; children inherit protection.
# The launcher programs were added on 2026-11-08 (unverified on Windows): like the game, in
# block mode each needs its relaxations, found one fatal block at a time as below.
protect \nexon_launcher.exe
protect \nexon_client.exe
protect \nexon_agent.exe
protect \nexon_runtime.exe
protect \MapleStory.exe
protect \DwarfAxe.exe
protect \CrashReportClient.exe
protect \NGService.exe
protect \grap-core64.aes
protect \grap-updater.aes
protect \grap-communicator64.aes

default-deny on
block-files on
block-registry on
block-volume-serial on
block-process-memory on
block-process-create on
block-raw-disk on
block-network on
block-network-adapter on
network-default deny
network-loopback off

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Identity: never relaxed (owner, 2026-10-31). Deny rules come before every relaxation and
# the first matching rule decides, so no allow below can open these.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
deny|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography|value=MachineGuid

# Relaxations, in the order they were found.

# Z1 (zero run 1, 2026-10-31): the new game copy never runs: the launcher and csrss get no
# access to it. Identity check: these give the launcher / csrss access INTO the game (resume
# its thread, its memory); nothing about the machine or user reaches the game. Requested rights.
allow|thread-handle|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Program Files (x86)\Nexon\Nexon Launcher\bin\nexon_client\nexon_client.exe|rights=0x1FFFFF|risk=cross-process-handle|uses=1
allow|handle|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Program Files (x86)\Nexon\Nexon Launcher\bin\nexon_client\nexon_client.exe|rights=0x1FFFFF|risk=cross-process-handle|uses=1
allow|handle|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\csrss.exe|rights=0x1FFFFF|risk=cross-process-handle|account=system|uses=10
allow|thread-handle|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\csrss.exe|rights=0x1FFFFF|risk=cross-process-handle|account=system|uses=6
# Z2 (zero run 2): csrss's follow-up read of the new game's memory (component context).
# Identity check: csrss reads the game; nothing about the machine or user reaches the game.
allow|handle|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\csrss.exe|rights=vm-read|risk=cross-process-handle|account=system|uses=1
# Z3 (zero run 3): the first copy exits (needs administrator) and Appinfo, the elevation service,
# starts the elevated copy for the launcher; launch pass now 2 starts. Identity check: who may
# start the game only; no data reaches the game.
allow|launch|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\svchost.exe|rights=create|account=system|uses=1
# Z4 (zero run 4): the elevated copy, started by Appinfo, is frozen the same way: Appinfo's and
# csrss's handles to it get nothing (csrss's Z1 rules raised to 2 uses, one per start).
# Identity check: access INTO the game by two Windows system processes; nothing reaches the game.
allow|thread-handle|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\svchost.exe|rights=0x1FFFFF|risk=cross-process-handle|account=system|uses=1
allow|handle|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\svchost.exe|rights=0x1FFFFF|risk=cross-process-handle|account=system|uses=1
# Z5 (zero run 5): 0xc0000142 while kernel32/KernelBase initialise; csrss's further opens of the
# elevated copy (session 1: full, full thread, query; session 0: query+read, query) were denied:
# csrss process rule above 2 -> 6 uses, thread rule 2 -> 3. Identity check: access INTO the game.
# Z6 (zero run 6): 0xc0000135, startup DLLs not found; each denied at its real location.
# Identity check: reading program code files reveals nothing (MachineIdLib.dll is the game's
# machine-ID library: its own reads stay filtered, incl. the identity denies above).
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\winmm.dll|rights=read|uses=1
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Nexon\Library\maplestorycw\appdata\WzMss.dll|rights=read|uses=2
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Nexon\Library\maplestorycw\appdata\MachineIdLib.dll|rights=read|uses=2|risk=machine-id-library
# auto (zero): DLL requests at their real location; identity: program code only.
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Nexon\Library\maplestorycw\appdata\WzMss.dll|rights=read,execute|uses=1
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Windows\System32\winmm.dll|rights=read,execute|uses=1
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Nexon\Library\maplestorycw\appdata\MachineIdLib.dll|rights=read,execute|uses=1|risk=machine-id-library
# auto (zero): DLL requests at their real location; identity: program code only.
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Nexon\Library\maplestorycw\appdata\nexon_api_x64.dll|rights=read|uses=2
# Z9 (zero run 9): 0xc0000022 right after WzMss/MachineIdLib load; the loader's read of the
# component-store settings key was denied (earlier evidence: this key causes exactly this error).
# Identity check: component-store settings only; no machine, network, hardware or user data.
allow|registry|\Registry\MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\SideBySide|rights=read,enumerate|uses=16|exact
# auto (zero): DLL requests at their real location; identity: program code only.
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Nexon\Library\maplestorycw\appdata\nexon_api_x64.dll|rights=read,execute|uses=1
# Z11 (zero run 14): 0xc00000a5 (bad impersonation level) after rpcrt4: csrss's further handle
# requests on the game were refused; its Z1 rules raised by the counts denied (process 6 -> 10,
# thread 3 -> 6). Identity check: the same csrss access into the game as Z1.
# auto (zero): DLL requests at their real location; identity: program code only.
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Nexon\Library\maplestorycw\appdata\CrashReporter.dll|rights=read|uses=2
allow|file|\Device\HarddiskVolume3\Nexon\Library\maplestorycw\appdata\libcurl.dll|rights=read|uses=2

# Z27 (zero run 27): 0xc0000142 in the DLLs' start-up code; first candidate: Windows' opens of the
# HKLM root key itself (full access asked, 19x). Exact: the root key object only; every key opened
# through it is still checked by its full path. Identity check: the root key holds no data; none.
allow|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE|rights=read,write,delete,rename,set-security,enumerate|uses=19|exact
# Z28 (zero run 28): 0xc0000142: ws2_32's start-up opens its settings key with write too (0x6B).
# Exact, requested rights, once. Identity check: protocol-catalog settings, no machine/adapter/user data;
# write is limited to this one key (an integrity matter, not identity). Network stays blocked.
allow|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\WinSock2\Parameters|rights=read,write,delete,set-security,enumerate|uses=1|exact
# Z29 (zero run 29): the same WinSock settings key under its other name (ControlSet001), same rights.
# Identity check: as Z28; none.
allow|registry|\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\WinSock2\Parameters|rights=read,write,delete,set-security,enumerate|uses=6|exact
# anchor: relaxations go above this line
